When a customer goes over their limit, the API returns HTTP 429 and tells them how long to wait. The limit applies per workspace, so all API keys in one workspace share a single budget. Ten keys in one workspace share one budget. [1]

**What they get back:** An HTTP 429 response with a `Retry-After` header. Over the limit, the API returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header giving the number of seconds to wait. [1]

**How they know when to retry:** They read the seconds value in `Retry-After`. Northwind's SDKs handle this automatically, so customers using them don't need to write retry logic. Our SDKs honour it automatically and back off exponentially. [1]

**Other details that matter:**
- Short spikes are tolerated. Short bursts of up to 2x the limit are allowed for 10 seconds. [1]
- Rejected requests don't use up quota. Rejected requests are not counted against the monthly event quota. [1]
- A 403 is not a rate limit. Endpoints marked "Not available" return HTTP 403 on that plan, not 429. [1] Customers on a plan without an endpoint should not retry it.
- Limits can be raised in some cases. Enterprise ingest limits on /v2/events and /v2/events/batch can be raised up to 3x the default by contract. [1] Temporary raises for a one-off backfill (up to 72 hours), on any plan that has the endpoint, can be granted by the DP on-call primary. [1]
- The legacy endpoint won't get more room. We will not raise them for anyone; customers should move to /v2/events, which every SDK released after March 2025 already uses. [1]

The source is an internal page. It says the public docs copy it on each release, so the customer-facing wording may differ slightly.

You don't keep trying indefinitely. The protocol gives you a 30-minute window before the result goes up the chain, and a 60-minute deadline for the result to reach the ordering clinician. Critical results must reach the ordering clinician within 60 minutes. [1] If that doesn't happen, the result goes to the medical director on call. [1]

To reach the on-call medical director, call the Halcyon answering service at 555-0144 and choose option 2. The answering service pages the on-call medical director and, if there is no callback within 10 minutes, pages the backup. [3] Don't text physicians' personal mobile numbers, since pages through the answering service are logged and timed, which is what the chart documentation needs. [3]

Document each step in the chart with the time and the person notified. Every critical result notification is documented in the chart with the time and the person notified. [1]

- Patients in the sliding-fee program still receive that program's discount.

**Northwind Labs** fixed the root cause in the invoice creation step. The duplicate invoices (INC-2340) happened when a payment-provider webhook timed out, the retry logic re-ran the billing batch, and invoice creation had no duplicate protection. The engineering lead's fix was to make invoice creation idempotent, keyed on workspace and billing period, and that shipped on October 8 [3]. The team also added a daily reconciliation report that compares invoices against charges [8]. An alert for webhook timeouts during billing batches is still open and due November 6 [8].

**Halcyon Health** fixed the reminder sender (IR-0412). The duplicates came from a September 2 scheduler cutover, when the old and new job runners were both active and neither checked whether a reminder had already gone out [2]. The fix is a reminder idempotency key built from patient, medication, and scheduled time, so a reminder whose key already exists is never sent again [2]. Halcyon also now requires a written runbook and clinical safety sign-off for scheduler cutovers [2], and treats patient-facing automation as a clinical system under the same safety review as clinical protocols [2].

Halcyon's offer is bigger in percentage terms: a 20% prompt-pay discount compared with Northwind's 15% annual-prepayment discount. Two caveats apply to the Halcyon figure.

- **Northwind:** The 15% applies to a Growth annual prepayment. The policy measures it against the first-year value at list price, which works out to about $12,240 a year on the $1,200 monthly plan [1]. A later memo confirms the 15% prepayment rate is unchanged for quotes issued from October 1, 2026 [4].
- **Halcyon:** The 20% applies to self-pay patients who settle the full bill at the time of service [2]. It does not apply to vaccines or injectables, which are already priced at cost plus administration [3].

Because the two discounts apply to different things (a software subscription versus a patient visit), the comparison is only a rough one. On the headline percentage, Halcyon's is larger.
